title: Component
description: A named unit of the design, its responsibility, and which requirements it satisfies. ⚠️ Added to the catalogue 2026-08-22 (#140) — the FIRST type added because authentic work demanded it rather than because a list named it. Stage 5, run against the 14 active requirements, could not express its own third exit criterion without it. ⚠️ DELIBERATELY MINIMAL: a name, a responsibility, and `satisfies`. Further links wait for authentic stage 7-8 demand (#41) — a field added now for an acceptance criterion nobody has written is the catalogue justifying itself again (#106).

responsibility.description: What this unit is responsible for, in one statement. ⚠️ NOT a description of how it works: the implementation is the code, and a second prose model of it is #8's dual-representation failure. This is the boundary — what falls inside this component and what does not.

satisfies.description: Which requirements this component satisfies. ⚠️ MANY-TO-MANY, which is why the edge lives here and not on the requirement: one component satisfies several requirements and one requirement needs several components. It is also what the stage-9 completeness gate reverses to find a requirement no component satisfies, and what #60's cascade traverses from an acceptance criterion.

implementedBy.description: Where the component lives, as content-root-relative or repository-relative paths. ⚠️ Paths rather than a trace field on purpose: code is not an artifact, and pretending it is would put the repository inside the planning model. A path here is a POINTER for a human, never something the lint resolves (#75 does not apply).

tags.description: Changing tags never invalidates an approval (#103).

x-ownsIrreducibleState.description: #41 applied before building, and the case is that FOUR consumers were already decided and none could be served. The traceability chain in notes.md names 'design component' three times and #38's sixteen omitted it, so the chain #16, #19, the stage-9 gate and #25 all rest on had a missing link.
x-ownsIrreducibleState.owns: A named design unit, its responsibility, and the many-to-many satisfies edge. A requirement cannot hold this: a requirement states what must be true, not what implements it.
traversedBy: stage-9 completeness gate — a requirement no component satisfies is an orphan
#60 cascade — its worked example is acceptance-criterion -> component
#19 role slicing — a handoff slice is over components

rejectedAlternatives.string field on requirement: #85's prose assumption in a different costume — a string cannot be traced, counted or flagged, and the orphan check needs traversal.
rejectedAlternatives.prose in an architecture document: Same failure. planning-content/stages/05-solution-design.md section 1 IS that prose, and no gate can read it.
rejectedAlternatives.scope-boundary: A scope boundary says what is OUT of scope, not what implements what.

x-unresolvableTraceTargets.description: #75: none. `satisfies` targets `requirement`, which is implemented and activated.
